text:
clara: Quick heads-up 10:151 - I'm opening a PR to harmonize SOC2 / audit retention language across API reference, Console UI, and SDK docs. Also adding a short playbook for Data Subject Request (DSR) exports (GDPR) and a localization note for EU customers. Need legal-approved copy and tiny SDK snippets (Python + Rust). Will post PR link shortly.

miguel: Can you include a minimal curl example for requesting an export? Ill add a Rust snippet and a short migration mapping note for event_type -> audit_event.category.

clara: Yes. Draft retention copy I used in the branch: "Customers can configure retention per customer account; default retention is 90 days. Audit exports created for legal or regulatory obligations are preserved according to applicable law." Tagging @jen for legal.

jen: Legal notes - please use this exact three-sentence block instead: "Retention is configurable per customer account. By default, audit records are retained for 90 days. Audit exports required for legal or regulatory obligations will be preserved in accordance with applicable law." Also replace any standalone use of "customer" with "customer account" to match the glossary.

luis: From localization: add a short blurb for EU customers: "EU customer accounts may have supplementary local retention requirements; consult the privacy page for regional details." Put this under "Regional considerations" and add internal link to the privacy FAQ.

miguel: Draft Rust snippet for the SDK section (very small):
```rust
// rust: basic audit export
let res = client.audit().export(from_iso, to_iso, Some("90d")).await?;
println!("{} events", res.items.len());
```

miguel: Curl example for the playbook: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/audit/export?from=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-01-02T00:00:00Z" -o export.json`

clara: Add a jq example to help QA and DSR handlers quickly check exported fields: `jq '.items[] | {ts:.timestamp, category:.audit_event.category, dsr_id:.metadata.data_subject_request_id}' export.json`

docs-bot: PR #5342 opened by clara: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5342 :bookmark_tabs:

jen: I can sign off on legal phrasing once the exact three-sentence block is applied and the glossary term swap is done. Also confirm that the GDPR/DSR example notes we redact PII by default on exports unless a legal hold is present.

clara: Will update the PR to use the legal block, add the EU localization blurb, include the Rust + Python snippets, and add a short QA checklist for exports (jq sanity, verify no signed_url leakage). Tagging infra for the export-agent minor bump. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
